tracks.narration: Rotate the whole picture. Does the dot product change?
Start with two vectors u and v. Compute their dot product and note the angle between them.
Multiply both vectors by the rotation matrix R of alpha. As alpha sweeps, both vectors swing together. Their dot product holds steady — the angle between them never changes.
Why? Because R transpose R equals the identity. The dot product is u transpose v — and the R cancels itself out inside.
Rotations are rigid motions. Lengths, angles, dot products — all invariant. The geometry travels with the vectors.
